turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Morning doctor. I'm his mother. This is Arjun, he is having fever and cough, please see him, he was up half the night.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hmm, one second, this screen has frozen again... sorry, what is the child's name? I didn't catch it.
[SEG0003] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Arjun. He turned four in January.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Arjun, four. Ok. Tell me, what brought you in?
[SEG0005] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The fever, and the cough with it. He is just not himself.
[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Fever is there from four days, doctor. I am the grandfather, I stay with them in the same house.
[SEG0007] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Papa, no. It started day before yesterday, so two days, not four.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, can you repeat that? I was typing the registration. Two days or four days?
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I am saying four days. From Sunday night he was warm, I remember, because the match was on.
[SEG0010] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Today is Thursday, no? Um, well actually I first checked the thermometer on Tuesday morning. So two days. You are mixing it with that cold he had last week.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right, so we are not sure, somewhere between two and four days. Arjun beta, how are you feeling?
[SEG0012] person_4 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is it the throat, or the cough that is bothering you?
[SEG0014] person_4 (PATIENT): Cough. Mama.
[SEG0015] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The cough is wet, more in the night, and the fever comes and goes. In the day he is a bit better.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): How high has the fever been? The number, if you have it.
[SEG0017] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Around midnight I thought the thermometer said one hundred and three... no, sorry, I looked again, it was one hundred and one point four Fahrenheit.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Before that, when I checked around ten, it was one hundred and three Fahrenheit. I saw the reading myself, doctor.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): So one hundred and three at ten, and one oh one point four around midnight. What medicine did you give?
[SEG0020] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Crocin. I gave two spoons... no, no, one spoon only, the 5 ml spoon. It is Crocin DS, so one spoon is two hundred and fifty milligrams.
[SEG0021] person_2 (DOCTOR): Two fifty milligrams, one spoon. How often? Say it again, I clicked the wrong tab.
[SEG0022] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Three times yesterday and once this morning, by mouth, every six hours. Not closer than that.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Morning I also gave Brufen, the ibuprofen, one spoon... wait, no. I am getting muddled. The pink bottle was Crocin only. I did not give Brufen.
[SEG0024] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Correct, only Crocin. We have not given ibuprofen at all this time.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any vomiting? Any loose motions?
[SEG0026] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting, and no loose motions.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Is he breathing fast? Any rash on the skin? Pulling at the ear?
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, no, nothing like that. He is playing a little in the afternoon. Only he is eating less.
[SEG0029] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, appetite is down since yesterday. He took some milk, that's all. He didn't want rice.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any old problems? Asthma, hospital admission, anything on the file? The file is slow to open.
[SEG0031] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No asthma, no admission. Last winter he had a bad cough and they did a chest X-ray. They said it was borderline, but they didn't start any medicine for it.
[SEG0032] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He was going to have his tonsils out... ah no, that was his cousin in Pune. Arjun himself has not had any operation.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): No surgery then. Any allergy to a medicine or anything else?
[SEG0034] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. No allergies that we know of.
[SEG0035] person_4 (PATIENT): I don't know.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): That's fine, beta. Come, let me look in your mouth. Big open.
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Throat is a bit red. Chest is clear, I don't hear any wheeze. Both ears look normal. Tummy is soft, no pain when I press.

[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Temperature now is thirty eight point two degrees Celsius. Heart rate one hundred and eighteen beats per minute. Breathing is twenty six a minute. Oxygen is ninety eight percent.
[SEG0039] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, is it pneumonia? They had said that X-ray was borderline, no?

[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): I don't think it is pneumonia. My impression is a viral fever with a cough, provisional, from what I see today. That old borderline X-ray doesn't mean he has a chest infection now.
[SEG0041] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So, antibiotic or we just wait?

[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): No antibiotic now. Continue the Crocin, 5 ml, that is 250 mg, up to four times in a day if the fever is there, with at least six hours between doses. And plenty of fluids, water, buttermilk, whatever he will take.
[SEG0043] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You want a blood test? We can go to the lab downstairs itself.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not today. If the fever is still there after three days, we might do a blood count.
[SEG0045] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if he becomes worse before that, what to do?

[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): If he is breathing fast, or very dull, or the fever is just not settling, come earlier, don't sit at home. Otherwise, if he is not better in three days, come back and see me.
[SEG0047] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You know the traffic from our side was terrible, we left at seven itself and still... anyway. Thank you, doctor.
[SEG0048] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thank you doctor. We will do as you said. Arjun, say thank you.
[SEG0049] person_4 (PATIENT): Thank you.
